appraisal_events.evidence: « aperçut tout d’un coup à quelque distance de lui une autre Rachel, un double d’elle, mais absolument différent et qui figurait une simple petite grue » ; les deux « poules » « avec des collets en fausse loutre, ayant à peu près l’aspect qu’avait Rachel quand Saint-Loup l’avait rencontrée la première fois » ; « une Rachel pareille à ces deux petites poules, une Rachel à vingt francs ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The station encounter splits Rachel into the idealized woman Saint-Loup has composed and a twenty-franc prostitute identical to the two cheap poules who hail her; the narrator supplies the corroborating detail himself (their look is the look Rachel had when Saint-Loup first met her), so the deflation is narrator-backed and not merely Robert's fancy.

appraisal_events.evidence: « cet enfer où il vivait, avec la perspective et la nécessité d’un mariage riche, d’une vente de son nom, pour pouvoir continuer à donner cent mille francs par an à Rachel » ; « sa liaison avec Rachel, au contraire, était ce qui l’avait mis un peu hors du monde, faisait qu’il y était moins coté » ; « les perles admirables de Rachel rapprirent à Robert qu’elle était une femme d’un grand prix, il la caressa, la fit rentrer dans son propre cœur ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator states outright that the liaison costs Saint-Loup his standing in the world and traps him in a ruinous economy he glimpses but cannot leave, and closes with the quiet irony of pearls he paid for reassuring him of her great price; the mixed polarity registers the narrator's explicit counter-move, crediting Saint-Loup's intelligence and refusing the cheap explanation of vanity in favor of love.

status_effects.explanation: Locally she is reduced to a twenty-franc grue interchangeable with two shabby poules in fake otter collars, her hundred-thousand-franc valuation exposed as Saint-Loup's construction rather than her worth.

Her hold survives the exposure: Saint-Loup cannot bring himself to question her, restores her to his heart intact, and in the closing exchange her reproach about his drinking is met with immediate compliance (« C’est entendu, partons »).
The narrator says plainly that the affair has put him somewhat outside the social world and made him less highly rated there, with the sale of his name in a rich marriage as its price.
He lives in an « enfer » he now sees an exit from yet cannot take, and his one moment of clear sight ends in suffering, nostalgia, unaskable questions, and a return to the interiorized idol.

ambiguities: The deflation of Rachel is staged through Saint-Loup's momentary perception in free indirect style, and the narrator suspends the metaphysical claim himself (« à supposer que la Rachel poule fût plus réelle que l’autre ») while adding that « elle n’avait démérité en rien » — so the passage endorses the social and economic exposure without fully certifying the twenty-franc Rachel as the true one.
